request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. (Independent run 3.)

concerns: Top PR-AUC is run 3 (0.7385), but run 5 (random forest, 0.7366), run 7 (0.7343) and run 3 are all within ~0.004, far below one SD (~0.06). They are statistically indistinguishable.

By the simplicity rule, no LightGBM run beats the simpler models by more than one SD. Logistic (0.6925) trails the best by about 0.046, which is less than one SD, so logistic is technically the simplest acceptable choice. However, the gain from trees is consistent across feature sets (+0.04 to +0.05). I pick RF as a compromise: it needs less tuning than boosting and is not worse than it.

Agent features add only about 0.003 to 0.03 PR-AUC, well within noise. They add 19 features, and the extra complexity is not justified. Run 7 (all, no agent) matches run 3, so I would prefer the no-agent set if simplicity governs. Run 5 is the best RF run but uses agent features. Either is defensible.

The label origin is undocumented, so PR-AUC of ~0.73 and ROC-AUC of ~0.94 may reflect label artifacts (for example rules derived from size or volume) rather than true fraud. Size features show little marginal effect (no_size is similar to all), which is mildly reassuring.
Fold SD of ~0.06 on 5,410 providers (~506 positives) means differences are noisy. With a queue of about 100 providers, precision@50 of ~0.78 is a better operational guide but is also noisy.

The calculation window is a single year with no temporal holdout, so there is a risk of leakage across providers sharing beneficiaries or physicians. Further hyperparameter search is unlikely to beat the noise.
